Subject: FinGrid POC — API header compatibility & routing contract

Hi team —

Quick summary: FinGrid is seeing intermittent 502/504s on short-lived POC requests from our JS SDK (browser -> proxy -> Redwood). The field logs point at a mismatch in how the SDK emits client metadata headers vs what the runtime expects for routing. They see a spike when sessions are created and then a subset of requests routed to the slower variant, causing timeouts.

What I need from Platform/Product/SE:
- Short-term mitigation we can ask FinGrid to enable (canary or routing hint) so the POC stays healthy through end of quarter demos.
- A technical explanation we can give their eng/procurement for why headers need normalization (they asked for this in the security questionnaire).
- An estimate for a small SDK patch (normalize header casing + fallback header) and a runtime safeguard to tolerate header-name variants.

Attached: fingrid-prod-logs-20261109.txt (sanitized), repro-steps.md (minimal repro I captured).

Annie — I copied procurement since they requested the compatibility note for the contract. Can you confirm whether enabling a routing hint on your side is acceptable for a short canary? If so we can propose dates.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: FinGrid POC — API header compatibility & routing contract

Marissa — thanks for the signal and the repro. I skimmed fingrid-prod-logs and the pattern looks like a header-normalization mismatch + session affinity mis-route: the client sets "X-Client-Meta" but the browser proxy upper-cases to "X-CLIENT-META" in one codepath. Our routing policy currently matches header-name-case-sensitively in the variant selector. That explains the subset of requests that end up on the slower fleet (low-throughput variant).

Immediate suggestions:
- Short-term: ask FinGrid to set the routing hint explicitly (X-Redwood-Routing-Hint: low-latency-v2) on the initial handshake. That will override selector behavior.
- Short-term SDK change (low risk): normalize outgoing header names to lower-case before the outbound proxy; add a fallback header X-Redwood-Routing-Hint-Alt with same value. I attached a step-by-step repro (repro-steps.md) where I reproduce locally.

I can draft the note for Annie describing the workaround + steps to flip the canary. If Platform can add a tolerance layer (case-insensitive header lookup) that avoids change on their side that would be the ideal fix.

Logan
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Annie Lopez <annie@fingrid.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinGrid POC — API header compatibility & routing contract

Thanks for the clear repro and notes. Quick technical context: our kernel selection + routing mesh historically performed exact-string header matches for routing hints to avoid ambiguous rules across multi-tenant variants. We can relax the match to case-insensitive for the routing hint header in the selector without changing the core matching semantics for other headers.

Proposed plan (platform side):
1) Short-term (48h): enable a case-insensitive lookup for X-Redwood-Routing-Hint in the selector on the demo cluster. This is a config flip; no model rebuild. I can roll this as a canary.
2) Medium-term (2 weeks): add a defensive layer in the request preprocessor to canonicalize header names to lower-case for a small set of routing-related headers (X-Redwood-*, X-Client-Meta). We'll ship a minor patch and a runtime flag.
3) SDK patch: agree with Logan — normalizing header names in the JS SDK is trivial. We'll coordinate the release with a short note.

I attached routing-policy-screenshot.png showing the variant selector rule referenced. To proceed with the canary I need:
- one example request-id or trace-id from fingrid traffic (so I can find and pin the request path)
- approval for a short maintenance window (15 min) to flip the selector on the demo cluster (I will monitor).

If Annie or procurement prefers, Platform can provide a formal compatibility note for the contract.

Karthik

Annie —

Appreciate the prompt turnaround here. Based on Platform + Logan's analysis the immediate path that causes the POC instability is header-name casing and the routing hint selector matching exactly. We have two coordinated mitigations:

Mutual Action Plan (short version):
- FinGrid: add X-Redwood-Routing-Hint: low-latency-v2 on initial handshakes for the POC (can be set at the proxy level).
- Redwood (Platform): flip selector to case-insensitive for routing hint on demo cluster (canary) — ETA: Nov 16 morning PT.
- Redwood (SDK): publish 0.14.1 with header normalization + alternate fallback header by Nov 20.
- Both: monitor 72h of demo traffic; Redwood to provide a short compatibility note for procurement and legal.

If you approve the plan I can create a short amendment to the SOW for the POC period and we can route it via DocuSign. I've attached a draft mutual-action-plan spreadsheet and included the HubSpot deal link below.
